source_refs.note: Exercise 11.3, Question 11: book page 296. The book prints no answers for Unit 11.

blocks.prompt: 11 (a) A quarterback throws a football with a position vector \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 20t\,\hat{i} + (20t - 4.9t^{2})\hat{j}\). Find the time of flight before it hits the ground.
blocks.explanation:
The \(\hat{j}\)-component is the height of the ball; it is on the ground when the height is zero.
Find: the non-zero time when \(20t - 4.9t^{2} = 0\).
Plan: factorise and discard \(t = 0\) (the throw).
steps:
Given: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 20t\,\hat{i} + (20t - 4.9t^{2})\hat{j}\) (metres, seconds); height \(y(t) = 20t - 4.9t^{2}\).
To find: the time of flight \(T\).
Method: solve \(y(t) = 0\).

Height zero
\[20t - 4.9t^{2} = 0\]
\[t(20 - 4.9t) = 0\]
\[t = 0 \ \text{ or } \ t = \dfrac{20}{4.9} = \dfrac{200}{49}\]
Why: a product is zero when one factor is zero; \(t = 0\) is the moment of the throw.

blocks.prompt: 11 (b) A quarterback throws a football with a position vector \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 20t\,\hat{i} + (20t - 4.9t^{2})\hat{j}\). What is the maximum height reached?
blocks.explanation:
At the highest point the ball moves horizontally, so the vertical component of the velocity is zero.
Find: that time, then the height at that time.
Plan: \(\mathbf{v}(t) = \mathbf{r}'(t)\); set the \(\hat{j}\)-component to 0; substitute into \(y(t)\).
steps:
Given: \(y(t) = 20t - 4.9t^{2}\).
To find: the maximum height \(H\).
Method: at the top the \(\hat{j}\)-component of \(\mathbf{v}\) is zero.

Time of the top
\[20 - 9.8t = 0\]
\[t = \dfrac{20}{9.8} = \dfrac{100}{49} \approx 2.04 \text{ s}\]
Why: before this time the ball rises (\(20 - 9.8t > 0\)), after it the ball falls.

Check
\[H = \dfrac{u^{2}}{2g} = \dfrac{20^{2}}{2(9.8)}\]
\[= \dfrac{400}{19.6} \approx 20.41 \text{ m}\]
using \(v^{2} = u^{2} - 2gH\) with vertical speed \(u = 20\) m/s and \(v = 0\) at the top.

answer_figure.alt: Parabolic path of the football from (0, 0) to about (81.6, 0), with the highest point at about (40.8, 20.41) marked at t = 100/49 seconds, and the landing time 200/49 seconds marked.
answer_figure.caption: Path of the football r(t) = 20t i + (20t − 4.9t²) j (original drawing)

blocks.prompt: 11 (c) A quarterback throws a football with a position vector \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 20t\,\hat{i} + (20t - 4.9t^{2})\hat{j}\). At which time did football reach its maximum height?
blocks.explanation:
This is the time at which the vertical velocity is zero, already found in part (b).
Find: \(t\) with \(20 - 9.8t = 0\).
Plan: solve, and compare with the time of flight from part (a).
steps:
Given: \(\mathbf{v}(t) = 20\,\hat{i} + (20 - 9.8t)\hat{j}\).
To find: the time of maximum height.
Method: the vertical velocity is zero at the top.

Solve
\[20 - 9.8t = 0\]
\[t = \dfrac{20}{9.8} = \dfrac{100}{49} \approx 2.04 \text{ s}\]
Why: as in part (b).

Check
\[\dfrac{100}{49} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{200}{49}\]
The ball reaches the top at exactly half the time of flight, as expected, because the path is symmetric about its highest point (on level ground).
blocks.final_answer: The football reaches its maximum height at \(t = \frac{100}{49} \approx 2.04\) s.
